children: is putting $8.5 billion behind its next major comeback effort, laying out a multiyear plan to modernize restaurants, improve operations and win back customers with new menu and beverage offerings.
The strategy, called McDonald's >NEXT, is designed to push operating margins into the low-to-mid-50% range by 2030 while delivering 250 basis points of restaurant-level efficiency improvements.
For franchisees, that efficiency target could be especially important.

McDonald's estimates the improvement would translate into roughly $100,000 of additional annual cash flow for the average U.S. restaurant, with most of the benefit eventually reaching the restaurant's bottom line. Management expects the investments to generate an approximately four-year payback for franchisees.

We are confident that executing across the key components of NEXT will unlock stronger restaurant economics, generate attractive returns for the company, our franchisees, and shareholders, and increase capacity to keep investing in growth, CEO Chris Kempczinski said.
McDonald's plans to invest roughly $5 billion through 2030, with the remaining $3.5 billion deployed through 2036 across restaurant modernization, technology and operational improvements.
Management expects those investments to contribute nearly 2.5 percentage points to systemwide sales growth in 2027, moderating toward roughly 2 percentage points by 2030.
McDonald's is also targeting free-cash-flow conversion in the mid-to-high-80% range by 2030 while reducing general and administrative expenses to 1.9% of systemwide sales.
The menu strategy is getting specific as well.
By 2030, McDonald's wants to gain 1.5 percentage points of chicken-market share and another 1.5 points in beverages while maintaining its leadership position in beef.

The significance of >NEXT is that McDonald's is putting measurable economics behind its turnaround rather than simply promising better value and innovation. The $100,000 restaurant cash-flow target could help secure franchisee support, while chicken and beverages offer additional growth beyond burgers. Investors should watch whether the projected efficiency gains actually materialize, whether franchisees achieve the promised four-year payback, and whether the investment translates into sustained traffic and sales growth rather than temporary promotional gains.

title: McDonald's Unveils Massive Restaurant Reset
